```{r}
# load the package
library(mylinreg)
library(ggplot2)
data(iris)
```

## Overview

This vignette demonstrates the usage of the `linreg()` function implemented in our package.
`linreg()` fits a linear regression model using ordinary least-squares and returns an S3 object of class `linreg`.
We test all implemented S3-methods: `print`, `plot`, `resid`, `pred`, `coef`, `summary`.
We use the built-in `iris` dataset for demonstration.

```{r fit-model}
mod <- linreg(Petal.Length ~ Sepal.Length + Species, data = iris)
```

## print() method
The print() method prints the model call and regression coefficients, similar to base-R lm print output.

```{r print-demo}
print(mod)
```

## coef() method
coef() returns named vector of regression coefficients.

```{r coef-demo}
coef(mod)
```

## resid() method
resid() returns the vector of model residuals $\hat{e} = y - \hat{y}$.

```{r resid-demo}
head(resid(mod))
```

## pred() method
pred() returns fitted/predicted values $\hat{y}$.

```{r pred-demo}
head(pred(mod))
```

## summary() method
summary() outputs model statistics: coefficient table (estimate, standard error, t-value, p-value), residual standard error $\hat{\sigma}$, and degrees of freedom.

```{r summary-demo}
summary(mod)
```

## plot() method
plot() produces two diagnostic plots with ggplot2: Residuals vs Fitted and Scale-Location.
The three observations with the largest absolute residuals are labelled.

```{r plot-demo, fig.width=7, fig.height=7, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
plot(mod)
```

## Compare against base lm (validation)
We can compare against built-in lm() to verify correctness of our implementation.

```{r compare-lm}
mod_lm <- lm(Petal.Length ~ Sepal.Length + Species, data = iris)
coef(mod_lm)
```
